papers.title: SEEK: Self-Evolution through Execution Knowledge for Agentic Robot Manipulation
papers.problem: Robots forget what they learn when a task ends, so they repeat the same mistakes on the next try.
papers.fix: The SEEK system keeps working procedures and their measured results, which lifts success from 19.7% to 48.0% over ten attempts.
papers.practicalUseCase: A robot that keeps its lessons gets better each try, so store action results between runs instead of starting fresh.
papers.limitation: The tests ran on one benchmark, RoboDojo, so real-world results may differ.

papers.title: PyRUA-Dex: Learning Programmatic Policies for Dexterous Bimanual Manipulation with Coding Agents
papers.problem: Robot hands need good human demonstrations to learn, but those demonstrations are scarce and hard to collect.
papers.fix: PyRUA-Dex lets coding agents write robot hand programs without demonstrations, and it reaches 81.0% success on DexJoCo.
papers.practicalUseCase: Coding agents can replace costly demonstration data, so try programmatic policies before you collect more demonstrations.
papers.limitation: The paper tests two simulated benchmarks and one bimanual robot platform, so other robots remain unproven.

papers.title: ROAM-Bench: Evaluating Embodied Active Spatial Intelligence through Evidence Verification
papers.problem: Robot tests often score only the final answer, so a lucky answer looks the same as real spatial skill.
papers.fix: Seven top models show two failures: right answers with unmet task needs, and wrong answers despite passing strong checks.
papers.practicalUseCase: A correct final answer can hide weak skill, so check the steps a robot took, not only its result.
papers.limitation: The benchmark has 250 tasks in 27 indoor simulated rooms, so it does not cover real homes.

papers.title: CONCOR: Benchmarking Contrastive Decoding for Visual Hallucination Mitigation Beyond Final-Output Performance
papers.problem: Tests of image-describing AI score only final answers, so they hide how each fix really changes the model.
papers.fix: The CONCOR benchmark shows some fixes favor correct answers, while others correct strongly but add more errors.
papers.practicalUseCase: Raising fix strength helps some methods and hurts others, so test each method before you turn the setting up.
papers.limitation: The paper gives no numbers for the gap, so the size of each effect stays unknown.

papers.title: Islamic Social Financial Instruments and Sustainable Community Development: Evidence Synthesis on Community Resilience
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Research on zakat, waqf, and sadaqah is scattered, so nobody knows how they build community strength together.
papers.fix: A review of 93 studies shows zakat gives short-term relief, waqf builds lasting assets, and sadaqah gives flexible emergency help.
papers.practicalUseCase: Each tool has its own job, so combine zakat, waqf, and sadaqah in one plan with strong governance.
papers.limitation: The review pools past studies from 2010 to 2025, so it adds no new field data.

papers.title: Determinants of Financial Inclusion in the OIC and OECD Countries: Are They Different?
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.institution: International Centre for Education in Islamic Finance
papers.problem: Many people in Muslim-majority countries still lack formal financial services, even though Islamic finance has grown for ten years.
papers.fix: Across 35 countries, income, schooling, institution quality, and internet access drive financial inclusion in OIC countries.
papers.practicalUseCase: OIC countries need more spending on digital systems, youth, women, and income, so Islamic banks should target those groups.
papers.limitation: The data covers 35 countries from 2005 to 2021, so it shows links, not cause.

papers.title: Examining the Impact of Waqf Literacy on Waqf Behaviour
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Waqf collection stays low, and it is unclear whether knowing about waqf makes Muslims give more.
papers.fix: Survey data from 642 Indonesian Muslims shows waqf knowledge raises attitude, social norms, and control, which then raises waqf intention.
papers.practicalUseCase: Teaching people about waqf raises giving indirectly, so waqf groups should fund education before they ask for money.
papers.limitation: The sample covers only Indonesian Muslims, so results may not hold in other countries.

papers.title: Trends and Determinants of Sustainability Sukuk Issuance: Evidence from Global Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Sustainability sukuk keep growing, yet nobody knew what drives the size of each issue.
papers.fix: Across 11,944 sukuk, equity-based contracts, longer debt terms, and USD or Euro pricing give larger issues.
papers.practicalUseCase: Costly second party opinions shrink issue size, so issuers should cut review costs to raise more money.
papers.limitation: The data ends in 2022, so newer market changes are not included.

papers.title: From Clicks to Credit: AI-Measured Halal Product Awareness and Halal Financing Depth across OIC Countries
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Banks do not know whether consumer interest in halal products leads to more Islamic financing.
papers.fix: In 16 OIC countries, halal search interest raises total Islamic financing, mostly through Murabaha and Ijarah.
papers.practicalUseCase: Online halal interest signals demand, so lenders should offer simple Murabaha and Ijarah products where search interest rises.
papers.limitation: The effect on Mudarabah and Musharakah is weak, and the study uses search volume as a stand-in for awareness.
